title: LINQ through exceptions
prompt: Update and its record types are supplied. Write public static List<string> Summaries(List<Update> updates). Return one line for each Arrived update, in the form "3 arrived", and one for each Finished update, in the form "Soup: 15 min". Keep the original order. Leave out any other kind of update. A Finished update with negative Minutes is a bug in the data: throw an ArgumentException for it.
hints: Three things can happen to an update: it becomes a line, it is left out, or it is rejected. Which updates get which?
Decide by the update's type, and check the Minutes of a Finished update before building its line.
Loop over the updates. Use is or a switch on the type, throw for Finished with Minutes below 0, and add nothing for other types.
checks: Practice.Summaries(new List<Update> { new Arrived(3), new Note("hi"), new Finished("Soup", 15) }).SequenceEqual(new List<string> { "3 arrived", "Soup: 15 min" })
Practice.Summaries(new List<Update> { new Finished("Sort", 0), new Arrived(0) }).SequenceEqual(new List<string> { "Sort: 0 min", "0 arrived" })
ThrowsArgument(() => Practice.Summaries(new List<Update> { new Arrived(1), new Finished("Soup", -1) }))
checkLabels: Arrived and Finished must each give a line, in order, and the Note must be left out.
No updates must give an empty list.
Zero is a real value: "Sort: 0 min" and "0 arrived".
A Finished update with negative Minutes must throw an ArgumentException.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Adds a line for update types that should be left out.
Quietly leaves out the bad update instead of rejecting it.

feedback: Go through the failing updates one at a time and decide by hand: line, left out, or rejected. Then compare with what your code does.
